subject: LumenPay activation prioritization — routing affinity request

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harper Chen <harper.chen@lumenpay.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: LumenPay activation prioritization — routing affinity request

Team — quick ask. LumenPay (Harper cc'd) is moving to contract and has made activation timing a gating item for their Q1 launch partner program. The commercial team has landed a $1.2M 12‑month commit if we can deliver a routing-affinity capability (customer-specific model routing + deterministic residency preference) within their activation window (live target: 2027-02-15).

Attached: high-level MAP and the draft SOW. Key asks:
- Prioritize a lightweight routing-affinity flag so requests from LumenPay are routed to their dedicated pool or a pinned model variant (fallback to default otherwise).
- Add a short-term residency preference so inference favors us-east dedicated capacity for first 90 days.

Why this matters: they will sign in the next 72 hours if we can commit to a reasonable delivery window (we don't need full determinism Day 1, but deterministic routing for 95% paths is required).

Asks: can Product + Eng evaluate and give a go/no-go + rough timeline today? Procurement is ready to accept the SOW with the prioritization note. HubSpot deal is LMP-2026-1123.

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 9:14 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — quick ask. LumenPay (Harper cc'd) is moving to contract and has made activation timing a gating item for their Q1 launch partner program...

Thanks for the context, Marissa. Quick clarifying Qs for Product/Eng before we flag internally:
- Does Harper's team need model-level routing (i.e., specific model hash) or tenant-level residency preference (region/pool)?
- Are we okay with an initial 'preference' that is soft (best-effort) vs hard deterministic routing?

Laura — can you advise on where this would sit in the roadmap and whether we can offer an SLA-like commitment for residency for 90 days? Markus — can you provide a ballpark of effort (spike + implementation) and any risk flags (telemetry, cache affinity, KV-store impacts)?

I'll hold off external commitments until we have internal alignment.

-Dylan

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenPay activation prioritization — routing affinity request

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 10:02 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the context, Marissa. Quick clarifying Qs for Product/Eng before we flag internally...

High-level technical read: this is feasible as a scoped feature with two phases.
Phase 1 (MVP, 3–4 week):
- Add tenant routing preference metadata on request headers and routing layer will prefer dedicated pool instances or a pinned variant.
- Best-effort residency preference: prefer us-east subpool for placement; no hard enforcement.
- No model compile or kernel changes required. Cache warmup will be manual (we can provide a cache-seeding endpoint).
Risks:
- KV cache cold starts for tenant-specific affinity can increase 95th percentile latency early; we should document warmup strategy.
- Telemetry will need an extra dimension (routing_reason) for debugging and post-mortem.
Estimated team effort: spike (3 days) + dev work (2–3 sprints) + QA (1 sprint). If we compress and approve a small scope (no hard determinism, only preference + fallback) risk is manageable and could land in ~6 weeks with a 2‑engineer focused effort.

If Product wants hard guarantees (no fallback), complexity jumps: we need placement locking and a rollout plan, estimate 3–4 months with orchestration and playbooks.

-Markus
Senior Engineering Manager | Serving Runtime
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenPay activation prioritization — routing affinity request

Thanks — this aligns with my read. Product note on tradeoffs and gating: 
- I can reprioritize a small slice into the activation board if Commercial secures firm contractual commitment that includes a modest engineering prioritization credit (we'll track as non-recurring engineering in the SOW).
- Acceptable Day 1 scope for Product: tenant-level routing preference + residency preference (best-effort) + cache-seeding API + telemetry tags.
- Acceptance criteria: requests from LumenPay include header X-RD-Tenant:LumenPay and >95% of routed requests prefer us-east-priority pool within 30 days of go-live.
- If contract requires deterministic routing with zero fallback, we need to scope as a multi-quarter project.

Action proposal: Marissa to get a signed SOW addendum (names the preference behavior, commit window and commercial credit). Once signed we will: (1) schedule a 3-day technical spike (Markus), (2) prioritize a 2‑engineer squad for 6 weeks, (3) assign CS owner for warm-pool plan (Monica).

I'll mark this as "ready to schedule" pending SOW.

-Laura
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
